effects: Every fetched page reaches validated terminal status before its rows are accepted. Failed full pages cannot replace an existing Parquet/CSV output.
Sized HTTP response reads request content decoding and close on EOF or BaseException, while zero reads leave the stream open.
Outstanding-page and estimated-byte accounting retains pending, buffered and emitting pages until consumed or discarded. Ready ordered pages drain before new admission.
Queued futures are cancelled on close/failure/interrupt, running requests finish under existing transport policy, and the public wrapper explicitly closes the scheduler.

limitations: The byte budget estimates decoded payloads, not process RSS. A completed oversized page may exceed it; an empty window admits one page for progress.
Closing cancels queued work; running Requests calls finish under the existing timeout policy.
